name: ClearCrumb – Cookie Consent & GDPR Cookie Banner
author: ClearCrumb

sections.description:
ClearCrumb shows a fast, accessible cookie banner and stores each visitor’s choice in their own browser.

  • Auto-blocking: your services’ scripts and embeds wait for consent, even on cached pages.
  • Switching? Import your settings from Complianz, CookieYes or Cookiebot.
  • A two-minute setup wizard: regions, scan, services, design.
  • Works with WPML, Polylang and TranslatePress.
  • Banner in 16 languages (EN, DE, FR, NL, ES, IT, PT, PL, SV, DA, FI, NO, CS, RO, AR, HE), picked from your site language, right-to-left included.
  • A cookie policy page that keeps itself up to date: [clearcrumb_cookie_policy], in English, German, French, Dutch, Spanish and Italian.
  • A cookie scanner that checks up to 50 pages and finds the services your site uses.
  • A Leak Test that shows what still loads before consent.
  • A Compliance Score from 0 to 100 that tells you what to fix.
  • A consent checkbox for Contact Form 7 and WPForms forms.
  • A consent log in your own database: proof of every choice, kept as long as you choose (30 days to forever), with hashed IDs and IPs, and a CSV export.
  • Region rules: GDPR opt-in for the EU, EEA, UK and Switzerland, US opt-out with Global Privacy Control.
  • Google Consent Mode v2 (basic and advanced), Microsoft UET Consent Mode, Meta Pixel and TikTok Pixel consent APIs and the WP Consent API.
  • Placeholders for blocked videos and maps, with a locally stored thumbnail and a “Load video” button.
  • A library of 155 common services with their cookies, so visitors see who is behind each choice.
  • Four banner layouts and six design styles, with a live preview while you edit.
  • Accept, Reject and Preferences with four categories: necessary, preferences, statistics and marketing.
  • Reject always looks exactly like Accept. Saying no is never harder than saying yes.
  • A floating “cookie settings” button and a [clearcrumb_preferences] shortcode, so visitors can change their mind at any time.
  • Small and quick: no jQuery, no external requests, the banner script loads deferred.
  • Settings export and import as a JSON file, to set up your next site in seconds.
  • WP-CLI commands: wp clearcrumb scan and wp clearcrumb log export.
  • A dashboard widget with this week’s consent rate.
  • Block-editor blocks: Cookie policy and Cookie settings link.
  • Keyboard and screen-reader friendly (WCAG 2.2 AA target).

ClearCrumb helps you meet cookie rules but is not legal advice.

For developers

window.ClearCrumb.get() returns the visitor's choice (or `null`), `ClearCrumb.has( 'statistics' )` checks one category, and `ClearCrumb.open()` opens the preferences. Every saved choice fires a `clearcrumb:consent` event on `document`.

Source code & build

Everything ships readable. The banner scripts and styles sit next to their minified copies (assets/js/guard.js, assets/js/banner.js, assets/css/banner.css). The admin app’s source is in src/admin/, with the build tools in src/tools/. To rebuild assets/admin/ and the .min files, run this inside the plugin’s src folder (Node.js 18 or newer):

npm install && npm run build

External services

ClearCrumb sends nothing about your visitors anywhere. Your server contacts two services only to fetch a video thumbnail for the placeholder that replaces a blocked embed, once per video, in the background:

  • YouTube (Google): when a page contains a blocked YouTube embed, your server downloads the video’s thumbnail image from i.ytimg.com. Only the video ID is sent. Terms of Service · Privacy Policy
  • Vimeo: when a page contains a blocked Vimeo embed, your server asks vimeo.com/api/oembed.json for the thumbnail address and downloads the image from i.vimeocdn.com. Only the video ID is sent. Terms of Service · Privacy Policy

The thumbnails are stored in your uploads folder and shown from your own site, so visitors’ browsers contact neither service before they consent.
sections.faq:
How do I change the banner’s look?

Pick a layout, a design style and a button colour under ClearCrumb → Banner. For anything more, add your own CSS in WordPress under Appearance → Customize → Additional CSS (or Styles → Additional CSS in the Site Editor), with selectors that start with #clearcrumb.

Where is the visitor’s choice stored?

In a first-party cookie named clearcrumb_consent on your own domain. A copy of the choice goes to your own database as proof (the consent log), with the consent ID and IP address shortened and hashed. Nothing is sent to anyone else.

How do I add a “Cookie settings” link to my footer?

Add the shortcode [clearcrumb_preferences], or give any link the class clearcrumb-open-preferences.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Switching from CookieYes, Complianz, Cookiebot, Borlabs Cookie, Real Cookie Banner, Cookie Notice or GDPR Cookie Compliance is now seamless: visitors who refused there are not asked again, and a “yes” carries over when the old cookie shows a click. The consent log marks these “Carried over”. On by default, for one year after the switch.
  • Old “cookie settings” links, buttons and shortcodes of those plugins open ClearCrumb.
  • Scripts held with Cookiebot, Complianz or CookieYes markup (data-cookieconsent, data-category, data-cookieyes) are held and released by ClearCrumb.
  • Google Tag Manager triggers on the old CookieYes and Complianz event names keep firing.
  • The dashboard warns when another consent banner is still on, with one-click Deactivate. The Compliance Score checks “only one banner”.
  • Banner and guard are smaller; the migration code loads only on sites that switched.

1.0.4

  • ClearCrumb Pro is out: the Pro buttons now say “Get ClearCrumb Pro” and lead to the pricing page.

1.0.3

  • New “Ask everyone again” button under Banner: every visitor chooses again after you change your services or policy.
  • Keyboard focus comes back after Accept, Reject or Save (to the link or button that opened the banner, else the floating button).
  • Microsoft Clarity now gets the consent signal on the first Accept and on every page for returning visitors.
  • Google Maps placeholders show a drawn map instead of a plain box, still without any request to Google before consent.
  • The Compliance Score counts a [clearcrumb_preferences] link, the Cookie settings block or a .clearcrumb-open-preferences link as a way to change your mind.
  • Themes and page builders (Elementor kits, Hello) can no longer repaint the banner switches and buttons, also on hover.
  • WP-CLI: wp clearcrumb log export exports every record the log keeps by default.

1.0.2

  • New option under Banner → Design: show a small “Powered by ClearCrumb” line in the banner (nofollow link). Off unless you switch it on.
  • The plugin author name on the Plugins screen links to clearcrumb.com/about/.
  • The Sunset style is now rose pink, so it no longer looks like Paper.
  • Admin dropdowns show their arrow again.
  • The floating “cookie settings” button now plays the ClearCrumb logo animation every 4 seconds (off for visitors who prefer reduced motion).

1.0.1

  • Consent log: you choose how long records are kept (30 days to forever, one year by default), and you can download the log as a CSV file.
  • Removed the Custom CSS field. Use WordPress’s own Additional CSS instead; your design settings stay as they are.
  • Works on PHP 7.4 again (the cookie domain check used a PHP 8 function).
  • The region check now reads only the location headers it needs, sanitized.
  • The source of the admin app and the build tools now ship in src/.

1.0.0

  • First public release.
